# Numbering level recovery controls

Generated by `python tools/numbering_level_recovery_fixture.py` using Python's
standard library and the original, independently authored rich-content control
in `numbering-definition-recovery/healthy.docx`. No application serializer,
third-party document engine, or native reference output is used to construct them.

The same numbering instance supplies healthy level-zero items before/after the
affected content and in a header. Level-one failures appear in the body, a table
cell and the header, around formatted text and pictures. `healthy.docx` removes
only the affected paragraphs' list participation and malformed declarations.
That is the explicit read-only approximation, not a native rendering oracle.

Variants cover duplicate numeric indexes (1 and 01), missing and out-of-range
indexes, malformed override indexes/start values, and mismatched child indexes.
Unit checks also reverse three competing declarations to ensure ambiguity never
selects an arbitrary first/last record. Strict opening still rejects affected
used levels; preview retains original package bytes and disables serialization.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.9.6, 17.9.8, 17.9.26 describe level definitions, overrides
and start overrides. The supplied PDF was inspected at pages 711–717. Missing
`ilvl` and nonnumeric values intentionally fail XSD validation. Duplicate indexes,
index 9 and mismatched child indexes pass XSD; schema success is not full semantic
or implementation support. In particular, §17.9.8 says conflicting child `ilvl`
shall be ignored. This formerly rejected case is now covered by the independent native override
controls and implemented using the reference application's empty-level normalization. The historical
fixture remains available; the seven malformed variants still require recovery.

Validation: nine packages / 36 XML views; 32 pass and four intentionally malformed
numbering parts fail. Browser checks compare full canvas pixels and line geometry
for all eight variants against the healthy control, plus the real read-only UI
and byte-exact original download. Existing linked/list editing regressions cover
supported numbering independently.

Update: conflicting but valid child indexes are now supported using the reference
application's empty-level behavior. Their former recovery-only case is covered by the native
`numbering-override-index` and `numbering-override-sequences` suites. The seven
remaining malformed/ambiguous variants continue to use read-only recovery.
